title: companions/1: ions that co-elute with a row of a unit-mass table, with the evidence of each pair
description: Written by features.companions@1 (crates/mzlab-feat/src/companions/): for every pair of rows within rt_tol whose nominal m/z difference fits an isotope step (+1, +2), an adduct of [M+H]+ or an in-source loss of the lists, or that only co-elute, an edge with the numbers behind it. An edge needs the Pearson of the heights over the files (min_corr, at least min_corr_samples files); a mass difference alone never makes one. No row is merged or removed. With iso_group on, an `isotopes` section groups M, M+1 and M+2 rows and flags spill-over (opt-in, absent otherwise). ids are the row ids of the table. ratio is the height of `to` over the height of `from` (the lighter row is `from`).

params.description: the parameters used: rt_tol, min_corr, weak_corr, min_corr_samples, da_tol, max_edges, adducts and losses (the nominal differences, Da)

counts.description: pairs = pairs of rows within rt_tol that are at least da_tol apart; isotope, relation and coelution = edges written; weak = a relation fits and r is between weak_corr and min_corr; untested = r not computed (too few shared files or a constant level); implied = co-elution edges left out because isotope and relation edges already link the rows, or a stronger one links the row to the same group; dropped = edges past max_edges after the implied ones are left out; the strongest (Pearson, then the rows) are kept (counted, never silent)

id.description: row ids of the table, one per row

companion_of.description: per row: the id of the parent it is a companion of (the best edge by r, then the smaller RT offset), null when none

companion_via.description: per row: the kind of the edge that gave companion_of

weak.description: candidates whose mass relation fits but whose r is below min_corr (null = not tested), with the same numbers

weak_dropped.description: weak candidates past the 200 listed; the listed ones are the strongest (|r| descending, an untested pair last, then the rows)

isotopes.description: Present only with iso_group. Every +1 and +2 pair of rows within rt_tol is judged: r under iso_min_corr is never an isotope; at +1 a ratio in the spill_min..spill_max band is spill-over (instrument channel, not an isotope); a ratio outside iso_ratio_min..iso_ratio_max (+1) or above iso_m2_max (+2) is rejected; the others are isotopes and join the group of their lightest row. No row is removed.

params.description: the rules used: iso_min_corr, iso_ratio_min, iso_ratio_max, iso_m2_max, spill_min, spill_max, da_tol, rt_tol

counts.description: pairs judged and their verdicts (isotope, spillover, rejected_corr, rejected_ratio, untested), groups and grouped_rows

iso_group.description: per row: id of the lightest row (M) of its isotope group, null when ungrouped

iso_step.description: per row: 0 for M, 1 for M+1, 2 for M+2, null when ungrouped

spill_of.description: per row: id of the M whose +1 channel this row is flagged as (spill-over), null otherwise; never set for a grouped row

r.description: Pearson of the heights over the files that measure both rows (the shape evidence)

relations.description: every relation that fits the difference, never one forced: isotope_p1, isotope_p2, adduct_* and loss_* names (adduct_nh4 and loss_nh3 both fit 17 Da)

parent.description: the row the other is a companion of; null for co-elution

rule.description: why that parent: the lighter row of an isotope step or adduct, the heavier row of a loss, the more intense row when both an adduct and a loss fit

r.description: Pearson of the heights over the files that measure both rows

rt_offset.description: RT of `to` minus RT of `from`, min

apex_shift.description: median apex of `to` minus apex of `from` over the files that detect both, min

ratio.description: height of `to` over `from` per file: median and range

carbons.description: isotope_p1 only: the carbons the M+1/M range implies at 1.08 % per carbon, an upper bound when N, S or Si add to it

hint.description: isotope_p2 only: M+2/M of at least 0.25, so Cl, Br or S is a reading to look at (evidence, no verdict)
